title: Study comparing single versus dual antiplatelet therapy in elderly patients or patients at risk of bleeding undergoing balloon surgery.
official: Single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy in elderly or HBR patients undergoing percutaneous intervention with drug-coated balloons (PICCOLETO IV-EPIC 38)
summary:
Main objective: The primary objective of the study is to verify the superiority of SAPT vs. DAPT in terms of Net Adverse Clinical Events (NACE), defined as the composite of MACE and clinically relevant bleeding events (BARC 2, 3 or 5) at 12 months.
We thus suppose that SAPT may provide similar benefits to DAPT regarding rate of MACE, and may offer improved net clinical benefit in terms of NACE due to reduced bleeding risk.
conditions: Patients with Stable or Unstable coronary syndromes who have undergone successful PCI
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Successful PCI with Essential Pro DCB just performed, in 1, 2 or 3 coronary vessels
2. De novo coronary lesions in vessels with diameter >=2.0 and <=4.0 mm (visual estimation)
3. Stable or unstable coronary syndromes
4. Informed consent to participate in the study given by the patient or impartial witness
5. Male and female patients age ≥ 75 years or at high bleeding risk
Exclusion criteria:
1. Stent implantation during index or recent (<6 months) procedure
2. History of asthma induced by the administration of salicylates or substances with a similar action, notably non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs)
3. History of gastrointestinal perforation, ulceration, or bleeding (peptic ulcer bleeding-PUBs) related to previous use of NSAIDs or anticoagulant medications, or intracranial hemorrhage
4. Acute gastrointestinal ulcers
5. Hemorrhagic diathesis (including known bleeding disorders or ongoing active bleeding)
6. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min)
7. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), with elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST > 2 x ULN or total bilirubin >1.5 x ULN)
8. Severe cardiac failure (NYHA grade III or IV)
9. Combination with methotrexate at doses of 15 mg/week or more
10. Patients with baseline neutrophil counts < 1500 cells/mm³
11. Breastfeeding women
12. Known (and untreatable) hypersensitivity or contraindication to aspirin, heparin, clopidogrel, paclitaxel or contrast media, or any of their excipient which cannot be adequately pre-medicated
13. Full-blown thyrotoxicosis
14. Patients with a very high risk of thrombosis
15. Pregnancy at the time of hospitalization
16. Patients participating in another clinical study in which an investigational drug or device was administered within 30 days of screening or within the 5 half-lives of the study drug, whichever is longer
17. ST-elevation myocardial infarction
18. Life expectancy <12 months
19. Left ventricular ejection fraction <30%
20. Visible thrombus at lesion site
21. Target lesion/vessel with any of the following characteristics: • severe and/or >270° calcification of the target vessel, also proximal to the lesion (intravascular imaging not mandatory); • left main stem stenosis >50%; • target lesion is in the left main stem; • chronic total occlusion with anticipated necessity of retrograde approach; • lesion is in a bypass graft.
